stories.title: Yamunanagar civic body hosts rally against single-use plastic
stories.summary: The Municipal Corporation of Yamunanagar-Jagadhri held an awareness rally at a local school on Constitution Day. Students educated citizens on the environmental impact of single-use plastic and reviewed fundamental duties under the Indian Constitution. The event was supported by an authorised agency of the corporation.

stories.title: Microplastic contamination detected in Kashmir lakes
stories.summary: Research from 2026 has identified thousands of microplastic particles in Dal and Nigeen lakes, with sediment contamination also reported in Wular lake. Experts are calling for sustained enforcement and public participation to address the growing environmental threat posed by plastic waste breaking down into microscopic particles.

stories.title: ProAmpac to close two US manufacturing plants
stories.summary: Packaging company ProAmpac plans to shutter facilities in California and Missouri. The closures will result in the loss of more than 130 jobs, according to state Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification filings.

stories.title: ProAmpac closing two packaging plants, cutting 134 jobs - Plastics News
ProAmpac trimming footprint in California, Missouri - Packaging Dive
Kerala continues single-use plastic ban implementation
stories.summary: The Kerala government banned the manufacturing, sale, storage and transportation of various single-use plastic products in 2020. The decision followed reports that the state generates nearly 45,000 tonnes of plastic waste annually. Officials continue to navigate the challenges of robust implementation and product availability.

stories.title: Delhi introduces deposit return scheme offering refunds for returned packaging - NewsBytes
Perak considers enforcement for polystyrene containers
stories.summary: Following a statewide ban on single-use plastic bags, the Perak government is weighing new enforcement mechanisms for polystyrene food containers. State officials noted that while prohibitions have existed for years, local councils have faced persistent operational hurdles in policing compliance.

stories.title: Perak warns of licence revocation for plastic bag ban offenders
stories.summary: Perak has fully enforced a ban on single-use plastic carrier bags at commercial premises since September. Local authorities are using warning notices before issuing compounds, with repeat offenders facing the potential revocation of their business licences. Guidelines are being finalised to ensure uniform enforcement across the state.

stories.title: rPET demand rises in Brazil and Mexico
stories.summary: Reduced availability of virgin PET and weaker local currencies are boosting demand for recycled PET in Brazil and Mexico. Trade measures and shipping delays have tightened virgin supply, while antidumping investigations into imports from Vietnam and Malaysia have added further uncertainty to the regional market.

stories.title: Global Plastic Resin Prices: Supply, Demand and Market Trends - Grand View Research
European polymer prices face supply and demand uncertainty
stories.summary: European polymer availability may remain restricted into early 2027 due to production difficulties and reduced imports. While feedstock indications suggest a potential reduction in olefin monomer prices, the market continues to navigate contrasting pressures. December settlements for the sector remain uncertain.

stories.title: ICIS analysis warns of recycled polyolefin supply gap
stories.summary: New analysis from ICIS indicates that domestic supply of high-quality recycled polyolefins will fall nearly 2 million tonnes short of Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation targets without significant investment. The European market for recycled plastics is currently entering a period of significant change.

stories.title: Seasonal tightness impacts recycled resin pricing
stories.summary: Seasonal bale tightness is currently reshaping pricing trends for recycled PET, HDPE and PP in the United States. ICIS experts are monitoring how supply constraints, trade policies and shifting demand are influencing the recycled resin market.

stories.title: Democrats prepare to challenge presidential tariff power
stories.summary: Democrats taking control of Congress in January 2027 may introduce legislation to limit presidential tariff authority. The proposed bills could have ripple effects on USMCA trade talks and potentially impact the HVAC industry.

stories.title: US aluminium trihydrate prices rise 0.89% in October as freight costs jump on Santos-Houston route - AL Circle
Recycled polyolefin supply may miss regulatory targets
stories.summary: Independent analysis by ICIS warns that domestic supply of high-quality recycled polyolefins will fall almost 2 million tonnes short of Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation targets without a significant acceleration in investment. Henkel and WWF Germany have also partnered to advance packaging circularity.

stories.title: Low-density polyethylene market sees growth in recycled solutions
stories.summary: The low-density polyethylene packaging sector is expanding due to evolving consumer preferences and new technology. Advancements in recycled linear low-density polyethylene are driving the trend toward sustainable flexible packaging, with the market positioned for continued upward momentum.

stories.title: AI sorting raises the bar for plastics recycling in Molise
stories.summary: RES has integrated optical sorting technology from Pellenc ST, enhanced by artificial intelligence, at its Pettoranello del Molise site. The company aims to recover more value from increasingly complex plastic waste streams by combining advanced sorting with mechanical recycling. A chemical recycling facility is currently under development.

stories.title: Scientist wins Lawrence Award for plastic-degrading enzymes
stories.summary: Gregg Beckham, a senior research fellow at the National Laboratory of the Rockies, has won the Energy Department's Ernest Orlando Lawrence Award. The honor recognizes his work turning plant waste and plastics into chemicals, including enzymes designed to break down PET bottles. He was one of nine recipients.

stories.title: Enzyme Breaks Down Redesigned Recyclable Thermoset Plastic - Intelligent Living
Artificially evolved enzyme targets thermoset polyester resins
stories.summary: A study in Science Advances demonstrates that an artificially evolved enzyme can break chemical bonds in thermoset polyester resins. These materials are currently difficult to recycle because they cannot be melted by heat. The research offers a potential alternative to incineration or landfill disposal for these durable plastics.

stories.title: All Reflex Cushioning Plants Now Run on Recycled Resin - PlasticsToday
Plastic recycling market projected to reach $84.86 billion by 2035
stories.summary: The global plastic recycling market reached $36.70 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow to $84.86 billion by 2035, according to market forecasts. Growth is driven by rising environmental concerns and stricter government regulations on plastic disposal. Asia Pacific currently holds a 35 percent market share.

stories.title: PackUK releases final 2026/27 packaging producer fees
stories.summary: PackUK has published the final 2026/27 fees for the United Kingdom's packaging extended producer responsibility regime. The charges, which apply from April 1, 2026, are available through the government's online calculator. Harder-to-recycle packaging carries higher costs under the current producer responsibility framework.

stories.title: Singapore Environment Council proposes expanded EPR framework
stories.summary: The Singapore Environment Council has proposed expanding the nation's extended producer responsibility framework to cover all packaging materials. The report recommends a phased rollout, eco-modulated fees, and public-private partnerships. The government intends to assess its existing beverage container return scheme before considering any broader implementation of these measures.

stories.title: UK packaging EPR fees exceed initial estimates
stories.summary: Confirmed 2026/27 EPR fees for most materials are higher than the illustrative estimates published in December 2025. This is the first year fees are modulated by recyclability. Wood and plastic saw the largest increases, rising by 131 pounds and 50 pounds per tonne respectively compared to earlier projections.

stories.title: Glass packaging fees remain lowest in UK EPR scheme
stories.summary: Glass accounts for 94 percent of glass placed on the UK market, with the lowest per-tonne fee of any major packaging material. British Glass says the low cost reflects the ease of recycling the material. Significant fee changes are expected to take effect in years three and four.

stories.title: Singapore landfill nears capacity as EPR expansion urged
stories.summary: The Singapore Environment Council is calling for extended producer responsibility to cover all packaging. The country's only landfill is expected to be full by 2035, and officials report that two in five items placed in shared recycling bins cannot be recycled.

stories.title: Delhi government plans deposit return scheme for ‘sin goods’ packaging - Packaging Gateway
Delhi considers deposit return scheme for tobacco packaging
stories.summary: The Delhi government plans to include khaini and gutkha packets in a proposed waste-return scheme. Consumers would pay a refundable deposit at the time of purchase and reclaim the amount upon returning empty packets. Plastic PET bottles are also expected to be covered under the new system.

stories.title: Industry groups urge EU to pause packaging EPR rules
stories.summary: EURATEX and 17 other European industry groups have requested that the European Parliament and the Council suspend EU packaging regulations until 2035. The coalition is seeking a delay to the implementation of the current packaging extended producer responsibility rules.

stories.title: Mexico's circular economy law lacks implementation rules
stories.summary: Mexico's General Law of Circular Economy established extended producer responsibility as a legal obligation for the packaging industry. Manufacturers and brands are required to finance recovery and redesign packaging. However, nearly a year after the law was published, the specific rules to trigger these obligations remain missing.

stories.title: Amcor and FluidSolids explore compostable rigid packaging
stories.summary: Amcor has partnered with Swiss materials technology company FluidSolids to evaluate fibre-based bio composites for rigid packaging closures. The companies plan to focus on performance, manufacturability and scale-up using FluidSolids' platform, which utilizes natural binders and cellulosic fibre waste designed to break down under home-composting conditions.

stories.title: Irish researchers explore straw-based packaging for fresh produce
stories.summary: The Sustainpack+ project at Teagasc Ashtown is investigating the use of cereal straw for sustainable packaging. Researchers are examining how the natural biopolymers cellulose and lignin, found in wheat and oat straw, can provide structural strength and protection against microbes for fresh produce applications.

stories.title: UK innovators launch polystyrene alternative packaging project - Printweek
Kraft paper honeycomb core market projected to expand through 2035
stories.summary: The global kraft paper honeycomb core market is entering a phase of structural expansion, according to an IndexBox report. Forecasts suggest a shift from traditional logistics toward higher-value industrial uses for the hexagonal cell material. The market is reportedly benefiting from more disciplined procurement and diversified supply architecture.

stories.title: US corrugated box prices remain stable in November
stories.summary: US corrugated box prices remained stable in November 2026 following a 1.02% increase in October. Seasonal demand from retailers and e-commerce companies continues to support industry activity. Steady procurement and the absence of major supply disruptions have prevented significant price fluctuations during the busy holiday period.

stories.title: Boreal Bioproducts and Emulco target PFAS replacement
stories.summary: Boreal Bioproducts and Emulco have partnered to develop bio-based barrier coatings for fiber-based food packaging. The project aims to replace plastics and address PFAS by combining forestry-derived SpruceSugar and vegetable wax-based AquaVeg. Laboratory testing is currently underway to evaluate the coatings for grease and water resistance.

stories.title: Karnataka AAR clarifies GST rate for paper bags
stories.summary: The Karnataka Authority for Advance Rulings held that paper bags supplied by Cistro Packaging LLP are classifiable under Tariff Item 48194000. The ruling confirms an aggregate GST rate of 5%, noting that the specific description for paper sacks prevails over general headings that would otherwise attract 18%.

stories.title: Recyclable High-Barrier Packaging: Nfinite and Amcor Develop Protective Paper Alternatives - Trend Hunter
Nfinite Paper wins sustainability award
stories.summary: Nfinite Nanotechnology received the Packaging Europe Sustainability Award 2026 in the start-up category for its high-barrier paper packaging. The material was developed in collaboration with Amcor to provide a sustainable alternative for flexible packaging. The award was presented at the Sustainable Packaging Summit in the Netherlands.

stories.title: PMEC India 2026 showcases pharmaceutical machinery
stories.summary: PMEC India 2026 is hosting industry professionals to explore developments in pharmaceutical manufacturing and production technologies. The event features an expanded two-venue format, co-locating with CPHI India to connect stakeholders across the pharmaceutical ecosystem, including machinery manufacturers, technology providers and engineering firms.

stories.title: Papel San Francisco marks 60 years of Perini technology
stories.summary: Papel San Francisco is celebrating a long-term collaboration with Valmet, which is marking the 60th anniversary of its Perini converting technology. The partnership has focused on integrating production systems and increasing efficiency, which the company claims has helped redefine how the market perceives tissue products.

stories.title: India bottling machinery market size projected to reach $1.1 billion by 2035
stories.summary: The Indian bottling machinery market reached $540 million in 2025 and is projected to grow to $1.1 billion by 2035. Filling and capping machines currently account for the largest share of the segment, with automatic systems representing 71% of the market.

stories.title: Packaging demand drives growth in doctor blades market
stories.summary: The global doctor blades market enters 2026 with a focus on precision components for printing and packaging converting. According to an IndexBox report, demand is driven by press utilization and line speeds as converters increase their capacity for high-graphics and flexible barrier packaging.

stories.title: Amcor (ASX:AMC): What Does Its Lightweight Packaging Update Mean for Material Efficiency? - Kalkine
Automatic strip packaging machine market report released
stories.summary: A new report on the global automatic strip packaging machine market provides data on competition, regional expansion and industry dynamics through 2032. The study outlines emerging growth pathways and market trends intended to assist industry players in navigating current sector developments and production requirements.

stories.title: Blister packaging machine market expects steady transformation
stories.summary: The global blister packaging machines market is entering a decade of transformation as pharmaceutical and medical device producers reassess automation and regulatory compliance. An IndexBox report notes that the market enters 2026 with more disciplined procurement behavior and a focus on unit-dose packaging capacity.

stories.title: Die-cutter market projected to grow through 2036
stories.summary: The die-cutter market is expected to expand at a 5.7% CAGR through 2036, according to Future Market Insights. Converters are increasingly investing in automated cutting, stripping and print registration technologies to improve production efficiency and manage the growing complexity of modern packaging formats.

stories.title: Arburg opens first overseas machinery assembly plant in China - Plastics News
Mars invests £161 million in Melton Mowbray site
stories.summary: Mars is investing £161 million to upgrade its Melton Mowbray factory for mono-PP pouch production. The company expects smart optical sorting technology to cut production waste by more than 50 percent. Local officials described the investment as a vote of confidence in the town workforce.

stories.title: SC tightens food labelling norms, says warning labels must appear separately on front of packaging - Moneycontrol.com
Supreme Court issues directions on front-of-pack warning labels for packaged foods - BMI
Tetra Pak introduces spoonable food carton
stories.summary: Tetra Pak has launched the Tetra Reva package, featuring a full-top opening designed for eating directly from the carton. The company says the pull-ring mechanism replaces traditional foil seals, while the non-round shape provides additional space for branding and product information.

stories.title: Lighter Boxes, Lower Costs: How Russian Board From CPM Helps Indian Packaging Makers Cope With Rising Raw Material Price
Coca-Cola Zero Sugar recall issued in Australia
stories.summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners Australia recalled specific 30-packs of Coca-Cola Zero Sugar after a production error led to cans being incorrectly labelled as Coca-Cola Classic. The affected products were sold across Queensland and northern New South Wales. The drink inside remains the sugar-free version.

stories.title: PepsiCo India has planned to invest Rs 868 crore to establish a new greenfield food manufacturing facility in Manapparai
Frozen food packaging faces new scrutiny
stories.summary: Following cyberattacks on European supermarket freezers, industry experts are advocating for stronger seals and puncture-resistant packaging to maintain integrity during temperature fluctuations. Companies are currently focusing on downgauging and recyclability, with food-safe recycled content identified as the next major challenge for the sector.

stories.title: Tetra Pak launches Tetra Reva carton package for spoonable foods - Packaging South Asia
Enjay Converters acquires New Method Packaging
stories.summary: Enjay Converters, a specialty packaging group controlled by an investor group led by Champlain Financial Corporation, has acquired Ohio-based New Method Packaging. The acquisition expands the group portfolio in the specialty packaging sector.

stories.title: Enjay Converters Ltd ("Enjay"), a leading specialty packaging group controlled by an investor group led by the Champlain
Banks back KKR acquisition of Logoplaste
stories.summary: Banks have lined up €550 million in loans to support the acquisition of packaging company Logoplaste by KKR. The financing package follows the private equity firm move to take control of the manufacturer.

stories.title: Qnity acquires Meridian electronics adhesives business
stories.summary: Qnity Electronics is acquiring Meridian Adhesives Group electronics business for $840 million. The deal aims to bolster Qnity portfolio in semiconductor packaging and AI hardware. The valuation relies on expected future growth, with successful integration and regulatory clearance still required to achieve those targets.

stories.title: Ball Corporation breaks ground on India can plant
stories.summary: Ball Corporation has begun construction on a two-line aluminium beverage can plant in Meerut, its third facility in India. Supported by long-term customer contracts, the site is expected to start production in 2029 to serve the northern Indian market.

stories.title: Haldyn Glass buys out joint venture partner
stories.summary: Haldyn Glass is acquiring the 43.2 percent stake held by Heinz Glas International in their joint venture, Haldyn Heinz Fine Glass, for Rs 45.1 crore. The deal makes the premium glass packaging manufacturer a wholly owned subsidiary of Haldyn Glass.

stories.title: Loop Industries raises $5.9M, names interim CEO amid India plant push - Dealroom
Haldyn Glass takes full control of HHFG
stories.summary: Haldyn Glass has completed the acquisition of Heinz Glas entire 43.2 percent shareholding in their joint venture, Haldyn Heinz Fine Glass. The subsidiary will continue to operate its existing manufacturing facility and maintain current customer relationships under the new ownership structure.

stories.title: Ball Corporation plans $300 million India expansion
stories.summary: Ball Corporation is building a third beverage can plant in Meerut for $300 million, with production scheduled for 2029. While cans currently account for about 3 percent of India packaged drink sales, the company estimates demand will nearly double by 2030.
